title: How Much Does a Gestor Cost in Spain? 2026 Price Guide
description: What a gestor or gestoría charges in Spain in 2026: monthly fees for freelancers, tax return, registration and extras, with typical ranges and hidden costs.
excerpt: Most freelancers pay roughly €30 to €120 a month for a gestor, but extras can double the bill. Here is what is included and what is not.
tldr: In 2026 a gestor for a self-employed person in Spain typically costs roughly €30 to €120 a month before VAT, with online services at the low end and face-to-face offices higher. Personal tax returns, registration and replies to tax office notices are usually extra, so ask for a price list.

segments.text: A gestor, or gestoría, handles the paperwork Spain requires from freelancers and small businesses: quarterly VAT and income tax filings, the annual return, registrations and correspondence with the tax office. Published prices vary a lot, so the useful question is what the monthly fee includes and what is charged on top.

content.text: How much does a gestor cost per month in Spain in 2026?

segments.text: For a self-employed person (autónomo) the monthly fee typically runs from about €25 to €60 for basic online services to €60 to €120 for standard face-to-face offices in 2026, before VAT. One price guide puts autónomo management at €35 to €200 a month across the market, and specialist services with tax planning and international clients can cost more, from about €100 to €250 or more.

items: Basic online service: roughly €24 to €60 a month, covering quarterly VAT and income tax forms and an annual VAT summary.
Standard service: roughly €40 to €120 a month, adding document handling, bank reconciliation and more invoices.
Premium or specialist: roughly €100 to €250 or more, including tax planning, international sales or representation before the tax office.
Typical annual cost for a freelancer using a traditional gestoría: around €800 to €1,500 in one estimate, and around €350 to €800 with an online service once extras are counted.

segments.text: The monthly fee usually covers the routine quarterly filings and a limited number of extra forms. Published lists of typical extras include:

items: Annual personal income tax return: roughly €30 to €150 depending on complexity.
Registration or cancellation as an autónomo, and census changes: roughly €30 to €250.
Replies to tax office notices or appeals: roughly €50 to €200, or an hourly rate.
Additional tax forms: roughly €20 to €60 each.
Employee payroll, if you hire: roughly €5 to €20 per payslip per month.

segments.text: Because the extras can add up, ask for the full price list before you sign and confirm whether the fee is fixed or depends on the number of invoices.

content.text: How much does it cost to file a personal tax return?

segments.text: Guides quote roughly €30 to €150 for a resident's annual Spanish income tax return, with simple returns at the low end. content.text: How much does a gestor charge to help with an NIE?

segments.text: The official government fee for an NIE is €9.84 in 2026, and professional help adds a service fee of roughly €100 to €500 depending on the route, plus any apostille, sworn translation or notary costs. Doing it yourself in person is the cheapest option but needs Spanish and an appointment, which is why many newcomers pay for help.

content.text: Is a gestor worth it for a freelancer?

segments.text: For most freelancers, yes, especially in the first year. The time cost and the risk of a wrong or late filing usually exceed the monthly fee. Our guide to

content.text: How do I choose an English-speaking gestor?

items: Confirm whether emails, calls and documents are in English, and who you actually deal with.
Ask what forms and how many invoices the fee covers.
Check how they handle clients outside Spain and EU VAT.
Get the extras list in writing.
Ask about the software they use, since new invoicing rules apply from 2027.

content.text: Online gestoría or a local office: which is cheaper?

segments.text: Online gestorías are usually cheaper because they have lower overheads, and they suit freelancers with straightforward finances and a modest number of invoices. A local office costs more but gives you a named person, face-to-face meetings and often better help with unusual situations such as foreign clients or several income sources. If English matters, check the language of the support in both cases, not just the website.

content.text: Are there changes coming that affect gestor costs?

segments.text: One price guide notes that new invoicing-software rules, known as Verifactu, become mandatory from 1 July 2027. Ask any provider you are considering whether their software will be compliant so you do not face a disruptive change midway through a year. Rules and deadlines shift, so confirm the current position with your gestor.
Prices change, so confirm the current fee with the gestor. This guide is general information, not tax advice.

faqs.q: How much does a gestor cost per month in Spain?
faqs.a: In 2026 roughly €25 to €60 a month for basic online services and €60 to €120 for face-to-face offices for a self-employed person, before VAT.

faqs.q: How much does a gestor charge for a tax return?
faqs.a: Roughly €30 to €150 for a resident's annual return, and often €100 to €200 for non-residents or more complex cases.

faqs.q: What extras do gestors charge for?
faqs.a: Registration or cancellation as an autónomo, replies to tax office notices, additional forms and payroll are commonly charged on top of the monthly fee.

faqs.q: How much does an NIE cost in Spain?
faqs.a: The official fee is €9.84 in 2026. Professional help adds roughly €100 to €500, plus any apostille, translation or notary costs.

faqs.q: Do I need a gestor as a freelancer in Spain?
faqs.a: It is not legally required, but most freelancers use one because filing mistakes and late filings usually cost more than the monthly fee.
